question: Should OpenClaw standardize these four built-in hosting profiles and the associated Plugin SDK readiness-provider contract in core once the dependent readiness layers are accepted?
rationale: This is a new public deployment/configuration and Plugin SDK contract, not a repair of established behavior; technical review cannot choose the permanent product boundary or decide whether profile policy belongs in core.

options.title: Accept a staged core contract
options.body: Land the readiness foundation first, then accept a narrowly rebased profile layer only after exact package-installed deployment proof is attached.

options.title: Keep readiness generic
options.body: Accept only reusable operator-selected readiness criteria and leave named hosting posture policy outside the core product for now.

options.title: Defer the profile catalog
options.body: Pause this feature until the RFC and owner boundaries have explicit maintainer approval and a supported release-test matrix.

recommendation.title: Accept a staged core contract
recommendation.body: Land the readiness foundation first, then accept a narrowly rebased profile layer only after exact package-installed deployment proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked implementation stack and can provide the technical contract and proof context for the maintainer decision.
